claims.claim_ar: تكرار عبارة «ما أُنزلَ إليكم / إليك» في الآية كأداة بلاغية (تَكْرار) لتوكيد مصدر التشريع وبيان تعدد المواضع التي نزل فيها التشريع ومقارنة موقف المخاطبين معها.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the phrase “ما أُنزلَ” (what was revealed) functions as a badi' (takrar) device to emphasize the source(s) of legislation and to foreground the contrast between what was revealed and the addressees' failure to uphold it.

claims.claim_ar: بناء الجملة النفيية والشرطية «لَسْتُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ حَتَّى تُقِيمُوا...» يقوم كقصر/حصر (حصر وقيْد) للحال والموقف: لم تُمنحوا منزلة الاعتبار ما لم تقيموا التوراة والإنجيل، والشرح القرآني والبلاغي يبيّن ارتباط الشرط والجزاء.
claims.claim_en: The negative-conditional construction (e.g. “لَسْتُمْ ... حتّى تُقيموا”) works as a restriction/qualification (hasr/qasr): the addressees are not 'upon' anything (i.e., entitled to standing/authority) until they establish the Torah and Gospel. Commentary treats the condition and its consequence as rhetorically united.
claims.needs_review_reason: Claim relies on Zamakhshari's discussion of conditional/resultado phrasing (e.g. «وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ»); further corroboration from other balagha tafsirs recommended.

claims.claim_ar: الآية تحتوي انتقالًا في مخاطَب الخطاب: بدءًا بخطاب مباشر إلى «يا أهل الكتاب» ثم ذكر مخاطَبٍ آخر (المخاطَب النبوي/المتلقي «إليك/ربك») — قراءة بلاغية ترى هذا كإلتفات/تغيير في جهة المخاطب (التِفات) لتعزيز التوبيخ والتوجيه.
claims.claim_en: The verse exhibits a shift of address (iltifat): it opens with a direct address to “O People of the Book” and then refers to the Prophet/addressee in forms like “إليك / ربك”. This shift functions rhetorically to reproach and to alternate between public admonition and direct instruction. Zamakhshari's phrasing about the Prophet reciting to them (e.g. «اتل عليهم وأنت محق صادق») supports reading the verse as involving shifts of addressee.
claims.needs_review_reason: Evidence drawn from Zamakhshari's commentary phrase about addressing/recitation; cross-checking with other classical rhetoricians (Jurjani/Sakkaki) advisable to confirm technical classification.

warnings: Provided source_chunks are all from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf). The task requested extraction from al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, and tafsir balagha sections; those sources were not supplied. Claims therefore are primarily supported by Zamakhshari's commentary and may need corroboration from the other requested authors.

Some rhetorical labels (e.g., iltifat vs. other forms of address-shift) can be interpreted differently by different writers; entries marked 'medium' confidence should be reviewed against additional tafsir/بلاغة sources.
